Bought health insurance today, covered from tomorrow? Usually no.

Most plans have an initial wait of roughly 30 days for illness. Some listed illnesses and pre-existing diseases can have longer waits. Exact timelines vary, so check the policy wording.

Save this.

“My employer cover is enough” is a risky myth.
Another big one: “If I hide an old condition now, I can fix it at claim time.”
Usually not. If it was diagnosed or treated in the last 36-48 months, disclose it. Exact window is policy-specific. Save this.

Flying to Europe soon?

For a Schengen visa, your travel medical insurance usually needs about 30,000 euros of medical cover, valid across the Schengen area, and repatriation cover.

Check the policy wording. #TravelInsurance

A sprained ankle abroad can turn into a very expensive hospital visit.

Travel medical insurance can cover hospitalisation, emergency treatment, and often medical evacuation.

Before you fly, save the assistance number and policy copy offline. Save this. #TravelInsurance

Cheapest plan = best plan.

Usually, a lower premium means something was trimmed: co-pay, sub-limits, room caps, or narrower coverage.

Compare protection first, price second. Check the policy wording.

Follow for one clear insurance idea a day.

“Insurance companies never pay claims” is a lazy myth.

Most claims are paid. The ugly part is this: many disputes start with non-disclosure, waiting periods, or exclusions.

Tell the truth, keep records, check the policy wording. Save this.

Picking a round number for term cover is guesswork.

A simple start: annual income × years left to retirement, + outstanding loans, - existing assets and cover.

That is closer to your family's gap. Ask me anything about health cover.

10-15x income is a starting point, not a formula.

Add home and personal loans. Add more if you're the only earner.

Then ask the real question: without your income, how will monthly expenses run?

Save this.

Deluxe room at admission can shrink your claim.

If your policy allows only a single private AC room, taking a higher room category can trigger proportionate deduction across the bill, not just room rent.

Check the room cap before admission. Save this.

Rs 5 lakh hospital bill. You have insurance. Still paying Rs 1 lakh yourself?

That is what a 20% co-pay does. It cuts every claim, not just the premium.

Cheaper premium can mean costlier claim day. Check the policy wording. Save this.

Medical emergency? In the first hour, do 3 things:
Save the insurer helpline and policy number on your phone.
Tell the hospital you have insurance and want cashless.
Ask the insurance desk to start pre-authorisation.
Save this.

Cashless approval is not final claim settlement.

At admission, you show your health card. The hospital sends a pre-authorisation request to the insurer or TPA. Approval usually comes with a sanctioned amount, which can change later when the final bill is reviewed.

Save this.

Wealth building starts after protection, not before.

One hospitalisation or the loss of an earner can undo years of saving.
Insurance is what keeps the rest of the plan standing when life interrupts it.

Follow for one clear insurance idea a day.

Your health cover can get smaller without changing at all.

Medical inflation usually runs ahead of general inflation, so a cover fixed years ago may buy less hospital protection today than you think.

Save this.

Marriage. Baby. Home loan. Job change.

These are not just life updates. They change your liabilities and can change your group cover too.

Insurance is not a one-time purchase. Revisit the setting when life changes. Save this.
